Great, Sandra — thanks for the details and the questionnaire.

Quick notes ahead of the kickoff:
- Backfill approach: we recommend a staged seed->bulk model. Seed the index with the high-value content (help center + billing + FAQs) to get immediate production quality gains, then run full backfill in waves with throttled ingestion. We'll provide a backfill recipe that uses prefix caching to reduce token costs during reindexing.
- Chunking: for long documents, adopt 512-token sliding windows with 128-token overlap for rerank-compatible retrieval; for short docs, 1 chunk per doc. This balances recall and rerank latency.
- Vector DB: we support multiple backends. For Brightline size and latency needs I'd recommend evaluating Pinecone for managed simplicity or Milvus for on-prem control. Weaviate is also an option if you plan heavy metadata filtering. We'll include a cost/latency matrix in the kickoff deck.

Attaching a short checklist and an example embed-mapping CSV. Can we add Priyom from our integration team and Marissa (CS lead) to ensure acceptance criteria and QA are captured?

Attachments: redwood-embed-rerank-checklist.pdf (pdf), embed-mapping-sample.csv (csv)

Looping in the CSM/runbook side. A few items I want on the kickoff agenda so we can lock acceptance gates:

1) Rerank evals: provide a 200-query seed set and gold labels for top-3 relevance. We'll run A/B with current Elastic+BM25 baseline -> embed+rerank. Acceptance: improvement in NDCG@3 and precision@1 with no >5% latency regression on 95th p.

2) Smoke tests: index sanity (doc counts, idempotent upserts), embedding drift checks, and sample queries for coverage.

3) Rollout plan: canary on 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on quality regression tied to the eval set.

4) Backfill ops: recommended windowing for the 18M docs (we'll propose 100k/day with parallel workers unless you prefer faster), plus throttling knobs for user-impact avoidance.

Hi team + Brightline — attaching a quick pros/cons snapshot per DB and expected median P99 token latencies for embedding/rerank flow. Highlights:

- Pinecone: managed, simplest to operate, predictable throughput. Good for SaaS; cost higher at scale. P99 query latency estimate: 35-75ms (depends on vector size + filters).
- Milvus: strong for on-prem and heavy custom ops, lower pure-storage cost if you have infra. Ops overhead higher. P99: 40-90ms.
- Weaviate: great metadata filtering and GraphQL convenience; scaling behavior depends on cloud provider. P99: 45-100ms.

Recommendation for Brightline: start with Pinecone for the canary (fast time-to-value) and evaluate Milvus for a future on-prem consolidation if cost becomes a driver. For backfill, use batched upserts at 10k vectors per job and validate vector counts after each chunk.

Attachments: vector-db-pros-cons.xlsx (xlsx)

—Ben
